:::{#exm-kernel-exponential}
#### The kernel, normalizing constant, and mode of an exponential density

The [exponential density](#def-exponential) with rate $\rate$ is $f(t) = \rate \ef{-\rate t}$ for $t \ge 0$, and $f(t) = 0$ for $t < 0$.
Its [kernel](#def-kernel) is $g(t) = \ef{-\rate t}$ for $t \ge 0$, and $g(t) = 0$ for $t < 0$,
and the [normalizing constant](#def-normalizing-constant) is

$$
\ba
c
&= \frac{1}{\int_0^{\infty} \ef{-\rate t}\,dt}
&& \text{(@thm-normalizing-constant-formula)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sb{-\ef{-\rate t}/\rate}_0^{\infty}}
&& \text{(antiderivative of } \ef{-\rate t} \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{1/\rate}
&& \text{(evaluate at } \infty \text{ and } 0 \text{)} \\
&= \rate.
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

The kernel is largest at $t = 0$,
so by @thm-kernel-same-mode the [mode](#def-mode) of $f$ is $0$.

:::
